items.stem: What is the primary purpose of a short-term (for example 13-week) cash forecast in treasury?

options.text: To anticipate the timing of cash inflows and outflows so liquidity shortfalls or surpluses can be managed in advance
options.rationale: Correct: a rolling cash forecast reveals timing gaps so funding or investment can be arranged ahead of time.

options.text: To replace the statutory financial statements
options.rationale: A cash forecast supports treasury decisions; it does not replace statutory reporting.

options.text: To calculate taxable profit for the period
options.rationale: Taxable profit is an accounting computation, not the forecast's purpose.
That is unrelated to the liquidity purpose of the forecast.

items.explanation: Correct: a rolling cash forecast reveals timing gaps so funding or investment can be arranged ahead of time.

items.stem: Which statements about managing financial risk in treasury are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A forward contract can fix the rate on a future foreign-currency payment to reduce FX risk
options.rationale: Correct: a forward locks the exchange rate, hedging the exposure.

options.text: Floating-rate debt exposes the borrower to rising interest costs if rates increase
options.rationale: Correct: floating-rate debt reprices with market rates, so cost rises when rates rise.

options.text: FX exposure disappears once an invoice is recorded in the accounts
options.rationale: Recording the invoice does not remove the currency exposure until settled or hedged.

options.text: Fixed-rate debt always costs less than floating-rate debt
options.rationale: Neither is universally cheaper; it depends on the rate environment.

items.explanation: Correct: a forward locks the exchange rate, hedging the exposure.; Correct: floating-rate debt reprices with market rates, so cost rises when rates rise.

items.stem: Why does treasury concentrate cash from many accounts into a central structure?

options.text: To improve visibility and use of cash, reducing idle balances and borrowing needs
options.rationale: Correct: concentration and pooling put cash where it is needed and cut idle balances and external borrowing.

options.text: To hide cash from the external auditors
options.rationale: Concentration is an efficiency measure, not a way to conceal cash.

options.text: To increase the number of bank fees paid
options.rationale: Pooling typically reduces, not increases, costs.

options.text: Because regulations forbid more than one bank account
options.rationale: No such rule exists; pooling is a choice for efficiency.

items.explanation: Correct: concentration and pooling put cash where it is needed and cut idle balances and external borrowing.
